To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the most efficient strains for biological removal of dyes from water are: for brilliant green – Erwinia spp.; for Evans blue – Polyporus pincipes, Pleurotus spp. and Erwinia spp..
the most effective bacterial strain for removal of brilliant green and Evans blue was Erwinia (s12) in semi-static samples.

the decolourization of the triphenylmethanes brilliant green and disazos Evans blue by bacterial (Erwinia spp. - s12) and fungal (Pleurotus ostretaus BWPH and Polyporus piceipes RWP17) strains is possible and that the toxicity of the by-products of the decolourizing process is lower than toxicity of the original dyes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the possibility of biological decolourization of dyes and toxicity of process by-products.
biological removal of dyes, which can be used in the textile industry.
the possibility of using dead biomass of fungi and bacteria for sorption of dyes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the decolorization of dyes is possible with both bacterial and fungal strains, and the toxicity of by-products is dependent on the strain, dye, and the incubation conditions.
the tested microorganisms can be considered as a potential source for biodegradation and bioremediation of dyes.
the decolourization of the tested dyes is possible and the treated dyes can be considered as not toxic for D. magna and L. minor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the best results of dyes removal were reached by fungal strains.

the best decolourization was reached in shaken samples, the most effective strains were Erwinia spp., Polyporus piciipes and Pleurotous ostreatus and decolourization of dyes was connected with decrease or no changes of toxicity of by-products.
decolourization of dyes by microorganisms is possible and can be connected with decrease of toxicity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
decolourization of dyes is possible with the use of biological methods.
biological treatment of dyes can decrease their toxicity.
biological decolourization of dyes can be used for wastewater treatment and that the toxicity of treated samples can be decreased to acceptable level.
